result.markdown: --- title: "[event_time()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Create a vector of event times. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_event_time.py#L499-L617){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python event_time(time, status, time_max=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `event_time()` creates a vector of event times that may be exact, or right-, left-, or interval-censored. It is a port of etd's `event_time()` and validates its input with the same rules, in the same order. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [time]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Non-negative event times (numbers or booleans, with `None` or `nan` for missing values). For interval-censored values, this is the lower end of the interval. Accepts a list, a NumPy array, or a DataFrame series. A single number is treated as a vector of length 1. [status]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Status codes, the same length as `time`: `"e"` (exact event), `"r"` (right-censored), `"l"` (left-censored), or `"i"` (interval-censored). It can be missing (`None`) only where `time` is missing. Codes are case-sensitive, and categorical input is rejected. [time_max]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Upper ends of the intervals, the same length as `time`. Must be missing for values that are not interval-censored, and greater than `time` otherwise. The default `None` sets all values to missing. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [EventTime]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The event-time vector. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `time` or `time_max` isn't numeric, or `status` isn't a character vector. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the lengths differ, or a value breaks one of the rules above. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} Errors carry two extra attributes: `check`, a stable identifier for the rule that failed (such as `"status_invalid_value"`), and `locations`, a 0-based integer array of the offending positions (empty when the rule isn't about particular positions). Only the first failing rule is reported, but with every location that breaks it. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#5d61a8ca .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw x = gw.event_time( time=[7, 5, 3, 2, None], status=["e", "r", "l", "i", None], time_max=[None, None, None, 4, None], ) x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 7 5+ 3- [2, 4] ``` ::: ::: To start from a data frame, name the columns in a formula (or with `Outcome.event_time()`) and pass `data=` to `fit()`, which works on every DataFrame backend: ::: {#48eb0b03 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl df = pl.DataFrame({ "times": [0.14, 0.15, 0.44, 0.76, 1.18], "status": ["l", "e", "e", "e", "r"], }) gw.Turnbull().fit("event_time(times, status)", data=df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` Turnbull (self-consistent NPMLE for interval-censored data) n atoms ambiguous iters converged 5 4 1 1 True ``` ::: :::
